newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - GEC straddle lights up dull market.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - GEC straddle lights up dull market.

text.p: The UK options market was relatively quiet on Friday with many dealers hesitant ahead of the May 1 British election, dealers said
"The market has been ticking over but there hasn't been a lot of volume. People probably won't do too much until the election is decided," one trader said.
The Labour Party, in opposition since 1979, is poised to defeat the ruling Conservatives in the May 1 ballot, according to the latest opinion polls.
One of the few significant deals of the day was a straddle in GEC Plc when a dealer bought 1,000 August 360 calls at 16p and simultaneously purchased 1,000 August 390 calls at 8-1/2p.
In this strategy, the spreader is hoping the share will move sharply up or down, as potential profits are largest if the underlying stock moves a great deal before the August expiry.

If GEC shares are trading anywhere between the two strike prices of 360p and 390p by expiry, both contracts will expire worthless, leaving the spreader with a maximum loss of 24-1/2p, excluding commissions.
But if GEC is below 360p or above 390 by expiration, a profit will be realised.
GEC was standing at 366p by 1405 GMT.
A straddle was also executed in Lloyds TSB Group when a dealer bought 400 June 550 calls and the same amount of 550 puts for a total cost of 45p.
Like the GEC spread, the dealer is hoping for a large movement in either direction for the underlying share which was trading at 553p.
